# Perform the non-constant variance (NCV) score test (deprecated)

<small>Source: [`man/performNCVTest.Rd`](https://github.com/DiogoRibeiro7/heteroTests/blob/main/man/performNCVTest.Rd) · Help: `?performNCVTest`</small>

The Cook-Weisberg score test for non-constant error variance, the diagnostic returned by `car::ncvTest()`.

## Usage

```r
performNCVTest(model, data = NULL, var_formula = NULL)
```

## Arguments

`model`
:   an object of class `lm`.

`data`
:   optional data frame the model was fitted to, in which `var_formula` is evaluated, as in [`performCookWeisbergTest`](performCookWeisbergTest.md). When `NULL`, the default, the model frame of `model` is used.

`var_formula`
:   optional one-sided formula giving the variance model, evaluated in `data` (for example `~ x1 + x2`). When `NULL` the fitted values are used. Before 0.15.0 `var_formula` was the second argument: a formula passed there by position is still read as `var_formula`, with a warning; that form stops working in 1.0.0.

## Value

An object of class `htest` containing the chi-square score statistic, its degrees of freedom and the p-value.

## Details

Let \(\hat{e}_i\) denote the OLS residuals and \(\hat{\sigma}^2 = \sum_i \hat{e}_i^2 / n\) the maximum-likelihood variance estimate. The test regresses the scaled squared residuals \(u_i = \hat{e}_i^2 / \hat{\sigma}^2\) on the variance regressors \(Z\) and computes half the explained sum of squares of that auxiliary regression. Under homoscedasticity and normal errors the statistic is asymptotically chi-square with degrees of freedom equal to the number of variance regressors.

With `var_formula = NULL` the fitted values are the sole variance regressor, matching the default of `car::ncvTest()` and Stata's `estat hettest`.

Because the divisor 2 is the null variance of \(\hat{e}^2 / \sigma^2\) under normality, the test is sensitive to non-normal errors; [`performKoenkerTest`](performKoenkerTest.md) provides the studentized variant, which is robust to non-normal kurtosis.

## Deprecated

`performNCVTest()` is deprecated since 0.14.0: use [`performCookWeisbergTest`](performCookWeisbergTest.md), which gained `var_formula` and is the one entry point for the Cook-Weisberg score test. With a variance formula, `performNCVTest(model, var_formula)` returns what `performCookWeisbergTest(model, var_formula)` returns; without one the two return the same statistic, degrees of freedom and p-value, and `performCookWeisbergTest()` labels the result as the Cook-Weisberg test. The old name still works, returns what it returned and warns.

## Weighted fits

On a fit with weights the test is computed from the Pearson residuals \(\sqrt{w_i}\, e_i\), so it tests whether the weights are adequate; see the section on weighted fits in [`performKoenkerTest()`](performKoenkerTest.md), which also covers weights estimated by [`fitWLS()`](fitWLS.md).

## Validation

Reproduces `car::ncvTest()` to within `1e-8` for both the default and the `var_formula` forms; see `tests/testthat/test-pass-a-reference.R`. Releases before 0.7.0 regressed the *absolute* residuals on the fitted values and reported a t statistic, which is a Glejser-type test rather than the Cook-Weisberg score test.

## Supported models

It accepts an `lm` and a `glm` with the Gaussian family and the identity link, unweighted
or with positive weights, a `fitWLS()` fit and, since 0.16.0, a rank-deficient fit, which it
tests on the estimable part of its design: it gives the value of the same model fitted without the
aliased columns. It refuses a `glm` of another family or link, a `survey::svyglm()` fit, a
fit with a zero weight, a coefficient that is not finite for another reason, and `data` that
lack rows or variables of the fit. Since 0.16.0 it is built on the model context, and also refuses
a multivariate `lm` ("needs a model with one response"), a fit whose coefficients, residuals or
weights were changed after the fit, and a fit with `model = FALSE` whose model frame, rebuilt
from the data it was fitted to, no longer holds its response, because those data changed after the
fit, with or without `data`. A fit with `model = FALSE` whose data are gone is tested on
`data` that give its response and fitted values, and refused without them. Without
`var_formula` the test reads nothing from `data`, which is checked as before: it must
hold the variables of the model and the row names of the fit; with it, `data` is read as by
[`performCookWeisbergTest`](performCookWeisbergTest.md). Which model each test accepts, and why, is set out in
[`test_results`](test_results.md), under *Supported models*.

## References

Cook, R. D., & Weisberg, S. (1983). Diagnostics for heteroscedasticity in regression. *Biometrika*, 70(1), 1–10. [doi:10.1093/biomet/70.1.1](https://doi.org/10.1093/biomet/70.1.1)

Fox, J., & Weisberg, S. (2019). *An R Companion to Applied Regression* (3rd ed.). SAGE.

## Examples

```r
 data(mtcars)
 m <- lm(mpg ~ wt + qsec, data = mtcars)
 # Deprecated: use performCookWeisbergTest(m) and
 # performCookWeisbergTest(m, var_formula = ~wt)
 suppressWarnings(performNCVTest(m, var_formula = ~wt))
```
